title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation

body: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are evolving from single-session tools toward long-term personal assistants that must adapt to individual users across tasks, contexts, and interactions. This shift makes memory a core requirement for personalization, since user preferences, goals, constraints, relationships, and past experiences are accumulated gradually and often change over time. Graph-based personalized memory provides a structured way to model such user information through explicit relations, temporal context, and evidence links. Such representations can model not only what an agent remembers about a user but also how memories are connected, revised, and retrieved to support personalized decisions. However, existing work remains fragmented across personalized agents and generic graph memory frameworks, making it difficult to understand the design space as a whole. This survey develops a lifecycle-oriented view of graph-based personalized memory for LLM agents. We organize existing studies around memory representation, memory evolution, memory retrieval, and memory evaluation. We further compare key design choices, discuss current evaluation practices, and open challenges in building reliable long-term personalized agents. This survey aims to clarify how graph-based memory can support adaptive, controllable, and user-centric LLM agents.
summaryZh: 该综述系统地探讨了图基化个性化记忆在大型语言模型（LLM）智能体中的应用，旨在支持其从单会话工具向适应个体用户的长期个人助理演变。文章提出了一个生命周期视图，围绕记忆表示、记忆演化、记忆检索和记忆评估组织现有研究，并比较了关键设计选择。此外，该综述还讨论了当前评估实践中的挑战，并指出了构建可靠的长期个性化智能体所面临的开放性问题，为该领域的研究和发展提供了清晰的框架。
